#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copies the current Hyprland, DMS and Alacritty config into this folder.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CFG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}"
STATE="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}"
# Claude Code keeps sessions per directory, named after its path with non-alphanumerics as "-"
CLAUDE_PROJECT="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects/$(printf '%s' "$REPO" | sed 's/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/-/g')"

echo "Saving config to $REPO"

# Hyprland: main config + files generated by DMS + screen-sharing portal config (without *.orig / backup leftovers), scripts if any
rm -rf "$REPO/hypr"
mkdir -p "$REPO/hypr/dms"
cp "$CFG/hypr/"*.lua "$REPO/hypr/"
cp "$CFG/hypr/dms/"*.lua "$REPO/hypr/dms/"
cp "$CFG/hypr/xdph.conf" "$REPO/hypr/"
[[ -d "$CFG/hypr/scripts" ]] && cp -r "$CFG/hypr/scripts" "$REPO/hypr/"

# DMS: settings, monitors, themes, browser css
rm -rf "$REPO/dms"
mkdir -p "$REPO/dms/config" "$REPO/dms/state"
cp -r "$CFG/dms/." "$REPO/dms/config/"
# Session state (current wallpaper, monitor profile, icon theme)
cp "$STATE/dms/session.json" "$REPO/dms/state/"

# Alacritty (DMS regenerates dank-theme.toml, but it is saved anyway)
rm -rf "$REPO/alacritty"
mkdir -p "$REPO/alacritty"
cp "$CFG/alacritty/"*.toml "$REPO/alacritty/"

# fish: config, functions, conf.d and universal variables (without the *.bak / *.broken leftovers)
rm -rf "$REPO/fish"
mkdir -p "$REPO/fish"
cp -r "$CFG/fish/." "$REPO/fish/"
find "$REPO/fish" \( -name '*.bak' -o -name '*.broken' \) -delete

# Cursor: theme, fallback theme and session variables (for apps not started by the compositor)
rm -rf "$REPO/cursor"
mkdir -p "$REPO/cursor"
cp "$HOME/.icons/default/index.theme" "$REPO/cursor/"
cp "$CFG/environment.d/90-cursor.conf" "$REPO/cursor/"
cp -a "$HOME/.icons/Hacked-Red" "$REPO/cursor/"

# Icon themes: Sweet-Red (set in DMS) and candy-icons, which it inherits from
rm -rf "$REPO/icons"
mkdir -p "$REPO/icons"
for t in Sweet-Red candy-icons; do cp -a "$HOME/.icons/$t" "$REPO/icons/"; done

# SSH agent (gcr-ssh-agent from GNOME): session variable
rm -rf "$REPO/ssh-agent"
mkdir -p "$REPO/ssh-agent"
cp "$CFG/environment.d/90-ssh-agent.conf" "$REPO/ssh-agent/"

# Claude Code sessions and memory for this repo
if [[ -d "$CLAUDE_PROJECT" ]]; then
    rm -rf "$REPO/claude"
    mkdir -p "$REPO/claude"
    cp "$CLAUDE_PROJECT/"*.jsonl "$REPO/claude/" 2>/dev/null || true
    [[ -d "$CLAUDE_PROJECT/memory" ]] && cp -r "$CLAUDE_PROJECT/memory" "$REPO/claude/"
fi

# Current wallpaper (only the one in use, not the whole folder; other files in wallpaper/ are kept)
wp="$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get("wallpaperPath",""))' "$STATE/dms/session.json")"
if [[ -n "$wp" && -f "$wp" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$REPO/wallpaper"
    cp "$wp" "$REPO/wallpaper/"
    echo "Wallpaper: $wp"
fi

echo "Done."

1:# Labels and Borders
3:HyprExpo can render workspace labels, separate selection labels, and distinct borders for current, focused, and hovered tiles.
60:## Workspace Labels
64:| `plugin:hyprexpo:label_enable` | bool int | enable workspace labels | `1` |
65:| `plugin:hyprexpo:label_text_mode` | string | `token`, `index`, or `id` | `token` |
66:| `plugin:hyprexpo:label_token_map` | string | comma-separated tokens by visible tile order; empty entries skip | empty |
67:| `plugin:hyprexpo:label_position` | string | `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-right`, or `center` | `center` |
68:| `plugin:hyprexpo:label_show` | string | `always`, `hover`, `focus`, `hover+focus`, `current+focus`, or `never` | `always` |
69:| `plugin:hyprexpo:label_font_size` | int | base font size in pixels | `16` |
70:| `plugin:hyprexpo:label_font_family` | string | Pango font family | `sans` |
71:| `plugin:hyprexpo:label_bg_enable` | bool int | draw a background bubble behind labels | `1` |
72:| `plugin:hyprexpo:label_bg_color` | color | label background color | `rgba(00000088)` |
73:| `plugin:hyprexpo:label_bg_shape` | string | `circle`, `square`, or `rounded` | `circle` |
75:## Selection Labels
77:Selection labels are optional overlays used by `hyprexpo:kb_select`. They let normal workspace labels stay stable while selection tokens use a separate map.
81:| `plugin:hyprexpo:selection_label_enable` | bool int | enable the separate selection-token overlay | `0` |
82:| `plugin:hyprexpo:selection_label_token_map` | string | comma-separated tokens by visible tile order; empty entries skip | `a,s,d,f,g,q,w,e,r,t,z,x,c,v,b` |
83:| `plugin:hyprexpo:selection_label_position` | string | label anchor | `top-right` |
84:| `plugin:hyprexpo:selection_label_color` | color | selection-token text color | `rgb(ffcc66)` |
88:Draws each window's app icon over its spot in the workspace tile. The icon comes from the window's `.desktop` entry (file name or `StartupWMClass` matching the window class; Chromium `--app` windows match by the URL in `Exec`), falling back to the entry of the process that owns the window. Icons are looked up in the GTK icon theme, `hicolor`, then `pixmaps`. The lookup index is built on first use and rebuilt on config reload, so a newly installed app or icon shows up after `hyprctl reload`. Windows that only partly fit in a tile get their icon in the visible part; windows outside the tile get none.

section='''## Workspace overview

`Super + Tab` opens [hyprexpo](https://github.com/sandwichfarm/hyprexpo) (a maintained fork
of the plugin dropped from `hyprland-plugins`) on both monitors: a 2x2 grid per monitor,
workspaces 1–4 on DP-1 and 5–8 on HDMI-A-1, empty ones included. Click a tile or press its
number to go there, arrows + Enter to pick one, Escape to cancel; windows can be dragged
between tiles. Settings and bind are in `hypr/hyprexpo.lua`.

The plugin is not managed by `hyprpm`: it is built by hand against `hyprland-devel` from the
Hyprland COPR (exact match for the installed Hyprland, no headers to build, no `sudo` for
`hyprpm`) and installed to `~/.local/lib/hyprexpo/hyprexpo.so`, which `hyprexpo.lua` loads
with `hl.plugin.load`. Build (and rebuild after every Hyprland update):

```sh
sudo dnf install hyprland-devel lua-devel
git clone https://github.com/sandwichfarm/hyprexpo /tmp/hyprexpo && cd /tmp/hyprexpo
# check out the commit pinned for your Hyprland version in hyprpm.toml (0.57.2: d54a70d)
git checkout d54a70dcb75bd6812dc4609815e57943eafa8f51
make -o check-lua LUA_PKG_CONFIG=lua hyprexpo.so
install -Dm755 hyprexpo.so ~/.local/lib/hyprexpo/hyprexpo.so   # install, never cp over a loaded .so
hyprctl plugin load ~/.local/lib/hyprexpo/hyprexpo.so && hyprctl reload
```

- `-o check-lua`: the fork requires Lua 5.5 (what upstream Hyprland 0.57 uses), but the COPR
  builds Hyprland against Fedora's Lua 5.4, and the plugin must use the same Lua as
  Hyprland. The plugin only calls Lua C functions that are the same in 5.4 and 5.5.
- A plugin built for another Hyprland version doesn't load. Until it is rebuilt (and the fork
  has a pin for the new version), `Super + Tab` falls back to the DMS overview; the same
  happens when the `.so` is missing (e.g. after `restore.sh`), and the plugin settings
  are skipped.
- `Hyprland --verify-config` doesn't load plugins, so the settings are skipped there too.
- Labels show the workspace number (`label_text_mode = "id"`), not the tile position.

'''
s=s.replace("## Cursor\n", section+"## Cursor\n",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n "Workspace overview\|hyprexpo.lua" README.md

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sets up Hyprland + DMS from this folder, also on a fresh Fedora install: installs the missing
# packages (DMS, Hyprland, Alacritty, fish...), then restores the saved config.
# Before overwriting anything, it backs up the current config to ~/.config-backups/<date>.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CFG="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}"
STATE="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}"
BACKUP="$HOME/.config-backups/$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
# Claude Code keeps sessions per directory, named after its path with non-alphanumerics as "-"
CLAUDE_PROJECT="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects/$(printf '%s' "$REPO" | sed 's/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/-/g')"
# COPRs: DMS (enabling it also enables its dependency repo avengemedia/danklinux, which
# ships quickshell, matugen, dgop, danksearch...) and Hyprland (the one recommended by the
# Hyprland wiki for Fedora)
DMS_COPR="avengemedia/dms"
HYPR_COPR="lionheartp/Hyprland"
HYPR_REPO_ID="copr:copr.fedorainfracloud.org:lionheartp:Hyprland"
# Installed with weak deps (DMS recommends cava, qt6ct, qt6-qtmultimedia...).
# breeze-icon-theme: breeze-dark is one of the fallbacks of the Sweet-Red icon theme.
PACKAGES=(dms danksearch matugen dgop alacritty fish zoxide gcr gnome-keyring
    breeze-icon-theme xdg-desktop-portal-gtk)
# Installed without weak deps: they pull a bar, a launcher and kitty, which DMS already covers
HYPR_PACKAGES=(hyprland xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland)

# Packages: only the missing ones, so on an already set up system nothing is asked
missing() { for p in "$@"; do rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "$p"; done; }
mapfile -t need < <(missing "${PACKAGES[@]}")
mapfile -t need_hypr < <(missing "${HYPR_PACKAGES[@]}")
if (( ${#need[@]} + ${#need_hypr[@]} )); then
    echo "Installing ${need[*]} ${need_hypr[*]} (needs sudo)"
    # dnf copr and dnf config-manager come from dnf5-plugins
    rpm -q dnf5-plugins >/dev/null || sudo dnf install -y dnf5-plugins
    sudo dnf copr enable -y "$DMS_COPR"
    sudo dnf copr enable -y "$HYPR_COPR"
    # The Hyprland COPR also ships quickshell and matugen; keep the versions DMS depends on
    sudo dnf config-manager setopt "$HYPR_REPO_ID.excludepkgs=quickshell,matugen"
    if (( ${#need[@]} )); then sudo dnf install -y "${need[@]}"; fi
    if (( ${#need_hypr[@]} )); then
        sudo dnf install -y --setopt=install_weak_deps=False "${need_hypr[@]}"
    fi
fi

# Validate the Hyprland config before touching anything
Hyprland --verify-config -c "$REPO/hypr/hyprland.lua" 2>&1 | grep -q 'config ok' || {
    echo "The saved Hyprland config is not valid, nothing was restored." >&2
    Hyprland --verify-config -c "$REPO/hypr/hyprland.lua" >&2
    exit 1
}

echo "Backing up current config to $BACKUP"
mkdir -p "$BACKUP/state"
for d in hypr dms alacritty fish; do
    [[ -e "$CFG/$d" ]] && cp -r "$CFG/$d" "$BACKUP/"
done
[[ -f "$STATE/dms/session.json" ]] && cp "$STATE/dms/session.json" "$BACKUP/state/"
mkdir -p "$BACKUP/cursor"
[[ -f "$HOME/.icons/default/index.theme" ]] && cp "$HOME/.icons/default/index.theme" "$BACKUP/cursor/"
[[ -f "$CFG/environment.d/90-cursor.conf" ]] && cp "$CFG/environment.d/90-cursor.conf" "$BACKUP/cursor/"
[[ -d "$HOME/.icons/Hacked-Red" ]] && cp -a "$HOME/.icons/Hacked-Red" "$BACKUP/cursor/"
for t in "$REPO/icons/"*/; do
    t="$(basename "$t")"
    [[ -d "$HOME/.icons/$t" ]] && mkdir -p "$BACKUP/icons" && cp -a "$HOME/.icons/$t" "$BACKUP/icons/"
done
[[ -f "$CFG/environment.d/90-ssh-agent.conf" ]] && cp "$CFG/environment.d/90-ssh-agent.conf" "$BACKUP/"
[[ -d "$CLAUDE_PROJECT" ]] && mkdir -p "$BACKUP/claude" && cp -r "$CLAUDE_PROJECT/." "$BACKUP/claude/"

# Hyprland
mkdir -p "$CFG/hypr/dms"
cp "$REPO/hypr/"*.lua "$CFG/hypr/"
cp "$REPO/hypr/dms/"*.lua "$CFG/hypr/dms/"
cp "$REPO/hypr/xdph.conf" "$CFG/hypr/"
[[ -d "$REPO/hypr/scripts" ]] && cp -r "$REPO/hypr/scripts" "$CFG/hypr/"

# DMS: config, session state, and started with the Hyprland session (dms.service is a
# systemd user service; `dms setup` normally adds this link)
mkdir -p "$CFG/dms" "$STATE/dms"
cp -r "$REPO/dms/config/." "$CFG/dms/"
cp "$REPO/dms/state/session.json" "$STATE/dms/"
systemctl --user add-wants hyprland-session.target dms.service

# Alacritty
mkdir -p "$CFG/alacritty"
cp "$REPO/alacritty/"*.toml "$CFG/alacritty/"

# fish (installed above, with zoxide used by config.fish): copy the config, make it the default shell
mkdir -p "$CFG/fish"
cp -r "$REPO/fish/." "$CFG/fish/"
fish_path="$(command -v fish)"
if [[ "$(getent passwd "$(id -un)" | cut -d: -f7)" != "$fish_path" ]]; then
    echo "Setting fish as the default shell (asks for your password)"
    chsh -s "$fish_path"
fi

# Cursor
mkdir -p "$HOME/.icons/default" "$CFG/environment.d"
cp "$REPO/cursor/index.theme" "$HOME/.icons/default/"
cp "$REPO/cursor/90-cursor.conf" "$CFG/environment.d/"
rm -rf "$HOME/.icons/Hacked-Red"
cp -a "$REPO/cursor/Hacked-Red" "$HOME/.icons/"

# Icon themes (Sweet-Red, set in DMS, and candy-icons, which it inherits from)
for t in "$REPO/icons/"*/; do
    rm -rf "$HOME/.icons/$(basename "$t")"
    cp -a "$t" "$HOME/.icons/"
done

# SSH agent (needs the gcr and gnome-keyring packages)
cp "$REPO/ssh-agent/90-ssh-agent.conf" "$CFG/environment.d/"
systemctl --user enable gcr-ssh-agent.socket 2>/dev/null || echo "Could not enable gcr-ssh-agent.socket (is gcr installed?)"

# Claude Code sessions and memory (resume with: claude --resume <session id>)
if [[ -d "$REPO/claude" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$CLAUDE_PROJECT"
    cp -r "$REPO/claude/." "$CLAUDE_PROJECT/"
fi

# Wallpaper: copied to the path session.json expects if it is missing
wp="$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get("wallpaperPath",""))' "$REPO/dms/state/session.json")"
if [[ -n "$wp" && ! -f "$wp" && -f "$REPO/wallpaper/$(basename "$wp")" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$wp")"
    cp "$REPO/wallpaper/$(basename "$wp")" "$wp"
fi

echo "Done. Hyprland reloads its config on its own (or run: hyprctl reload); for DMS: dms restart"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds the hyprexpo workspace overview plugin (github.com/sandwichfarm/hyprexpo) for the
# installed Hyprland and installs it to ~/.local/lib/hyprexpo, where hypr/hyprexpo.lua loads it.
# Run by restore.sh; run it again after every Hyprland update.
# Needs hyprland-devel (same version as hyprland) and lua-devel.
set -euo pipefail

sudo dnf install --setopt=install_weak_deps=False hyprland xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland hyprland-devel

start=s.index("The plugin is not managed by `hyprpm`")
end=s.index("- Labels show the workspace number")
s=s[:start]+'''The plugin is not managed by `hyprpm`: `hyprexpo.sh` builds it against `hyprland-devel`
from the Hyprland COPR (exact match for the installed Hyprland, no headers to build, no
`sudo` for `hyprpm`) and installs it to `~/.local/lib/hyprexpo/hyprexpo.so`, which
`hyprexpo.lua` loads with `hl.plugin.load`. `restore.sh` runs it (and installs
`hyprland-devel`, `lua-devel` and `make`). After a Hyprland update:

```sh
sudo dnf upgrade hyprland hyprland-devel   # both must be the same version
./hyprexpo.sh                              # then log out and back in
```

- The script takes the Hyprland commit from the `hyprland-devel` headers, checks it matches
  the installed `Hyprland`, and builds the plugin commit the fork pins for it in
  `hyprpm.toml`. It doesn't build anything when there is no pin yet for a new Hyprland
  version (try again later).
- It does nothing if the plugin is already built for the installed Hyprland (the commit is
  saved in `~/.local/lib/hyprexpo/hyprland-commit`); `./hyprexpo.sh --force` rebuilds anyway.
  Building takes about 2 minutes.
- If the running Hyprland is the one it built for, it loads the new plugin right away and
  reloads the config (the stack layout re-tiles open windows).
- It is installed with `install`, never `cp`: writing over a loaded `.so` crashes Hyprland.
- Lua: the fork requires Lua 5.5 (what upstream Hyprland 0.57 uses), but the COPR builds
  Hyprland against Fedora's Lua 5.4, and the plugin must use the same Lua as Hyprland. The
  plugin only calls Lua C functions that are the same in 5.4 and 5.5, so the script skips
  the fork's version check (`make -o check-lua`) after checking that `lua-devel` is the Lua
  Hyprland links.
- A plugin built for another Hyprland version doesn't load. Until it is rebuilt, `Super + Tab`
  falls back to the DMS overview; the same happens when the `.so` is missing, and the plugin
  settings are skipped.
- `Hyprland --verify-config` doesn't load plugins, so the settings are skipped there too.
'''+s[end:]

EOF

content.text:
Listo, ya está en el repo (commit `4f3fa6b`, sin push). Ahora `restore.sh` instala todo lo que hace falta y compila hyprexpo.

**Qué agregué:**
- **`hyprexpo.sh`** (nuevo): compila e instala el plugin. Toma el commit de Hyprland de los headers de `hyprland-devel` y se fija que coincida con el Hyprland instalado. Después busca en el fork la versión del plugin que corresponde a ese commit y lo instala en `~/.local/lib/hyprexpo/`.
- **`restore.sh`**: instala `hyprland-devel`, `lua-devel` y `make`, y después corre `hyprexpo.sh`. Si Hyprland ya está instalado, pide el `hyprland-devel` de la misma versión. Si la compilación falla, `restore.sh` sigue igual y `Super+Tab` queda con el overview de DMS.
- Actualicé el README y `CLAUDE.md`.

**Qué probé:** corrí `hyprexpo.sh` en un HOME temporal. Compiló bien en unos 2 minutos y, al correrlo de nuevo, no recompiló porque ya estaba al día. La config da `config ok`.

**Qué no probé:**
- Correr `restore.sh` completo en una instalación nueva.
- El caso en que el script recarga el plugin en la sesión abierta, después de recompilarlo para el Hyprland que está corriendo. Eso hace `hyprctl reload`, así que el layout stack reacomoda las ventanas abiertas.

**Cuando actualices Hyprland:**
```sh
sudo dnf upgrade hyprland hyprland-devel
./hyprexpo.sh    # después cerrá sesión y volvé a entrar
```
Hasta que lo recompiles, `Super+Tab` vuelve al overview de DMS. Si el fork todavía no tiene una versión para el Hyprland nuevo, el script te avisa y no compila nada.

Dejé sin commitear la línea de DMS en `hypr/dms/input.lua` (la del touchpad del joystick), `session.json` y las sesiones de Claude, porque no tienen que ver con esto. Si querés, los sumo en otro commit.
